source.title: MDM-Prime-v2: Binary Encoding and Index Shuffling Enable Compute-optimal Scaling of Diffusion Language Models
source.authors: Chen-Hao Chao; Wei-Fang Sun; Jun-Wei Quan; Chun-Yi Lee; Rahul G. Krishnan

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present. Some equations and figure/table layouts are flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures loss across model, data, and compute scales and fits a Chinchilla-style scaling law, but applies this analysis to masked diffusion models and reports training loss rather than testing the original held-out-loss setup directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports training loss, not held-out pretraining loss, so it does not test V1 as worded. It fits a scaling estimator and extrapolates compute-optimal allocations, but does not show that a power law fitted on small runs predicts the loss of much larger runs (V2). Scaling plots and fit coefficients, compute-optimal allocation exponents, architecture-shape comparisons, downstream loss/accuracy results, and the 7B allocation projections are included. Benchmark comparisons against reference models, sample-quality metrics, and attention/spectral analyses are not direct results for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study runs Chinchilla-style isoFLOP scans and fits a parametric loss law (14M–3.4B parameters, 3e18–3e20 FLOPs, C4). It does this for an autoregressive baseline and for masked diffusion LMs, a new model family, and reports fitted exponents and compute-optimal splits. It also reports shape-invariance and loss–downstream relations. These results bear directly on V1, V3, V4, V6 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also stress that ARM's split favours parameters (â 0.52) while MDM and MDM-Prime-v2 favour data relatively more (both 0.50). They claim the techniques improve accuracy on all eight benchmarks, but their own Table A7 shows ANLI falling with Technique 1. Their headline conclusion is that MDM-Prime-v2 beats similar-sized baselines at 1.1B.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Chinchilla-style fit to loss over model and data scales, but tests masked diffusion and related model families on C4 and reports training loss. It does not reproduce held-out-loss extrapolation tests from small runs.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported fit coefficients and compute-optimal exponents differ by model family. Tested shape comparisons report little performance sensitivity across the three depth/width configurations. The downstream accuracy response varies by benchmark and technique setting.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The scaling plots provide no exact plotted loss values in the text, and the reported scaling analysis uses training loss rather than held-out loss. The paper does not independently validate loss predictions from small runs on much larger runs. The shape comparisons are figure-only, and no uncertainty is stated for the Table 2 allocation exponents.
record.rows_left_out: No direct scaling-claim results omitted. Reference-model benchmark comparisons, sample-quality results, attention-pattern analyses, and singular-value results were left out because they do not directly measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Held-out loss is not reported (training loss only). The compute range spans only ~2 orders of magnitude, and no goodness-of-fit is reported.
All of it. The fit is extended to 1e25 FLOPs but never checked against a larger run; the 7B run is not compared to a prediction.
Stability across datasets, tokenizers or fitting methods (only one fit on C4 with GPT-2 tokenizer). No uncertainty is given on the allocation exponents.
Only three depth/width shapes, only for MDM-Prime, only over 20K steps. Other architecture details are untested for loss, apart from embedding-merge variants.
All of it: no other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer regime.
Downstream versus model size across a scaling series. The loss–accuracy evidence is over training steps, token granularity and technique ablations at 170M, plus a 3-checkpoint 7B run.

missing.what: 7B MDM-Prime-v2 downstream accuracy versus training tokens (0.2T/0.5T/1.2T): SciQ 90.67→92.67→92.67, PIQA 55.33→57.33→59.33, ARC-C 26.00→28.67→30.00. Bears on downstream improvement with data scale.
T1-only versus T1+T2 comparison: loss 2.34→2.31, but TruthfulQA 28.4→26.6 and McTaco 65.9→64.9 fall. Current rows use only the 2.63 baseline, hiding this.
IsoFLOP curves for each family (loss vs N at fixed C from 3e18 to 3e20), the data underlying the allocation fit.
Irreducible-loss and scale coefficients E, A, B per family (e.g., E = 2.029 / 2.420 / 1.578). Needed to compare fitted laws.

record.verdict_notes: V5 was removed from the rows: a masked-diffusion objective on text is a language-model setting, not another modality or regime of the kind V5 names. Those results were relinked to V1. A Chinchilla-style analysis applied to a new model family on C4 is a T3 setting; it is not T2, since the method is the original fit and the setting is new. Allocation projections (r16–r18) are untested extrapolations. Loss values across families are on different objectives and not comparable; only exponents are.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports training loss, not held-out pretraining loss.
It fits loss using empirical (loss, N, D) triplets and extrapolates optimal allocations, but does not test whether fits from small runs predict losses of much larger runs.
It tests fitted compute-optimal exponents for ARM, MDM, and MDM-Prime-v2 and gives projected token counts for target model sizes; other datasets and fitting setups are not tested.
Depth and width are varied at fixed model size. Other architecture details are not tested in this comparison.
The tested regime is text pretraining with masked diffusion models. Other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, and transfer are not tested.
The study examines ARC-e and eight commonsense benchmarks in the reported settings; it does not test broad downstream predictability across models, datasets, or task families.

It compares fit parameters and optimal-allocation exponents across ARM and diffusion model families. It does not vary parameter-counting conventions, schedules, datasets, or fitting methods, nor report a test of curves bending away from a power law.

relationships.condition: ARM, MDM and MDM-Prime-v2 on C4, 14M–3.4B params, 3e18–3e20 FLOPs, training loss
relationships.reason: Loss falls consistently with compute for all three families (r1–r3). A Chinchilla power law fits with α≈0.31–0.38 and β≈0.33–0.38 (r10–r15). Evidence is figure-only and on training loss, with no fit-quality statistic.
relationships.display_finding: Training loss decreases with compute for all three families, with fitted parameter exponents approximately 0.31–0.38 and token exponents 0.33–0.38.
